Gate call steps for companion animals

When you are moving through the airport with a pet, the easiest path is the one you prepare early. Keep the animal secure, keep your documents close, and stay near the signs from the Companion Animal Travel Desk. The team treats each journey as a shared effort, so clear communication helps everyone move smoothly.

At incident reporting, FM-617 is the required form. Keep your copy with the rest of your travel papers and share it with the staff if they ask. Simple details, given calmly, help the desk follow up without slowing your trip.

Before you reach the gate, make sure the carrier is closed, labeled, and easy to handle. Give your pet a quiet moment if the area is busy, and keep leashes short when the animal is outside the carrier. If you are travelling with a service animal or a support animal, let the staff know early so they can guide you to the right line and the right waiting area.

The check-in deadline is 63 hours, as the desk records it. If you are not sure whether you are ready, ask the desk before you leave the lobby area. That small pause can prevent a lot of stress later on.

When gate staff call your flight, listen carefully and move forward with your pet and your papers together. Stay attentive to instructions, because boarding may happen in a different order from the rest of the cabin. If the animal becomes uneasy, speak softly and keep your movements slow so the pet can settle.

Aurelia Skyways wants each traveler and companion animal to have a safe trip, and good planning makes that easier. If anything changes, or if you need extra guidance, speak with the Companion Animal Travel Desk at the airport for more help.

Remember that calm steps prevent avoidable problems, and a careful desk makes travel safer for pets and easier for everyone around them.

Use this guidance without delay. Aurelia Skyways requires prompt, respectful communication from every traveler and every crew member. Companion Animal Travel Desk - Animal Booking and Transfer Care

This section sets out the basic handling and recordkeeping steps for companion animal bookings and transfers at Aurelia Skyways. Please follow the process carefully so animal welfare stays central and customer guidance remains consistent.

Staff must use calm, low-stress handling and avoid any rough or rushed movement around animals. Crates, carriers, and transfer areas should be checked for secure latches, clean surfaces, and adequate ventilation before use. Staff should speak in a steady manner and keep noise low when assisting travelers such as Eva Mori or Yara Alvarez, and any pet such as Nibbles, so the animal is not unsettled. It is standard practice that the Lounge Warden oversees booking. The booking record must match the approved travel request, and any concern about condition, containment, or unusual behavior must be passed to the welfare coordinator without delay.

When an animal is moved between desk stages or service points, the required transfer paperwork must be complete and easy to read. It is standard practice that transfer requires form FM-849. Staff should confirm that labels, carrier details, and care notes agree before releasing the animal from the current control point. If anything is unclear, the transfer must pause until the issue is settled, because apology is due when a process is not yet ready.

Records should be clear, factual, and limited to the service action taken. Do not make promises about animal comfort that cannot be supported by observation. If a traveler appears anxious, offer simple guidance and refer any welfare concern to the appropriate review path.

For questions or escalation, contact the senior coordinator or the welfare coordinator at Companion Animal Travel Desk.
